summary_en.motivation: To enhance the fatigue performance of porous metallic biomaterials fabricated by Selective Laser Melting for load-bearing orthopaedic implants.
summary_en.method: The study systematically investigates the effects of process parameters, post-processing, and pore architecture on fatigue life using experimental characterization and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Optimized processing significantly improved fatigue resistance, and design guidelines for long-life porous structures were established.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through high-cycle fatigue tests, micro-CT analysis, and fractographic examination of as-built and post-processed specimens.

papers.title: Characterization of 316L Steel Cellular Dodecahedron Structures Produced by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: The compression behavior of different 316L steel cellular dodecahedron structures with different density values were studied. The 316L steel structures produced using the selective laser melting process has four different geometries: single unit cells with and without the addition of base plates beneath and on top, and sandwich structures with multiple unit cells with different unit cell sizes. The relation between the relative compressive strength and the relative density was compared using different Gibson-Ashby models and with other published reports. The different aspects of the deformation and the mechanical properties were evaluated and the deformation at distinct loading levels was recorded. Finite element method (FEM) simulations were carried out with the defined structures and the mechanical testing results were compared. The calculated theory, simulation estimation, and the observed experimental results are in good agreement.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the compression behavior of selective laser melted 316L steel cellular dodecahedron structures with varying densities.
summary_en.method: Fabricated single unit cells and sandwich structures with different cell sizes, conducted compression tests, and performed finite element simulations.
summary_en.result: Experimental, theoretical, and simulation results showed good agreement in mechanical properties and deformation behavior.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through mechanical compression testing and finite element simulation comparison.
